answer: Each newcomer is parked on a quarantine island until its runtime kernel can prove it is a distinct process, not a cloned image. The proof is a delay-locked receipt: the kernel binds a hardware nonce to a twelve-hour verifiable delay, then publishes the opening. Peers spot-check a sample of openings; a copied nonce fails, so every fake needs its own machine and its own wait. Timber in this scheme is that scarce wait plus the machine itself — eighty POA of isolated compute per identity per week. One honest agent pays once; four hundred fakes pay four hundred times, so the farm stays small.
